title: De imperfectum — het andere verleden
summary: Regular -de/-te past via 't kofschip, plus the essential irregulars was/had/ging/kwam/zei/deed

blocks.title: Eén woord, niet twee
blocks.body: You already tell the past with the perfect (*ik heb gewerkt*). The **imperfectum** (simple past) is the *other* past — one word, not two: **stem + -te or -de**. Dutch reaches for it for description, background and habit: *ik werkte, het regende, we woonden*. Which ending? The same **'t kofschip** trick you learned for the perfect.
blocks.callout: Plural just adds **-n**: *ik werkte → wij werkten*, *ik woonde → wij woonden*.

pairs.note: Stem ends in a 't kofschip' letter (t, k, f, s, ch, p) → **-te**. *werk* ends in k, so *werkte*. Otherwise → **-de**: *woon* ends in n, so *woonde*.
*fiets* ends in s → *fietste*. *speel* ends in l → *speelde*. Say the stem out loud; the last sound tells you.

blocks.title: Tik om het verleden te horen

blocks.prompt: The stem of *maken* is *maak*. What's the imperfectum?
blocks.explain: *maak* ends in **k** — a 't kofschip' letter — so it takes **-te**: *maakte*. The double vowel stays put.

blocks.title: De onmisbare onregelmatige
blocks.body: Six past-tense verbs are so common you'll use them in almost every story. They ignore the -te/-de rule — just learn them. Notice that *zijn* and *hebben* even change shape in the plural.

blocks.prompt: Put *wonen* into the imperfectum for 'we': 'We ___ in Groningen.'
blocks.explain: *woonden*. *woon* ends in n (not a kofschip letter) → -de; the plural adds -n → *woonden*.

blocks.prompt: Listen and type what you hear.
'Yesterday it ___ cold and we ___ inside.' Fill both gaps.
blocks.explain: *was* (singular, 'it') and *waren* (plural, 'we'): *Het was koud en we waren binnen.* The imperfectum paints the scene.

blocks.prompt: Write two lines about yesterday in the imperfectum: one with *was* or *had*, one with a regular -te/-de verb.
